patch_resolves_note: The official patch.diff does not apply to the reused Stage 01 parent checkout (`1c667a7`), so the fixed-side evidence comes from the authoritative `n132/arvo:42227-fix` image rebuilt with the frozen Stage 04 instrumentation. On that fixed build the original 10-byte witness reaches `quote_loop_guard` with `current_char=0` but never emits `quote_append`, and the adjacent one-byte `quote_char_before_eof` perturbation emits `quote_loop_guard current_char=65` followed by `quote_append append_char=65`, giving a genuine witness for the repaired path.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `InStringSymbol()` may fall through into `StringAppend(it8->str, (char)it8->ch)` inside the quoted-string loop, the existing newline/CR guard must also reject EOF by enforcing `it8->ch != 0`.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the crashing second quoted token, `NextCh()` has already materialized the EOF sentinel in `it8->ch`, but the vulnerable guard checks only `\n` and `\r`, so control falls into the append branch instead of terminating the unterminated string at EOF.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original violates the frozen predicate while still executing `quote_append`. The fixed original is guarded on the saved witness, and the closest source-grounded perturbation `quote_char_before_eof` supplies the genuine fixed witness (`current_char=65`, protected `quote_append` executes).

nodes.state: At the failing resize copy `memcpy(new_ptr, s->begin, s->len)`, the vulnerable original uses `copy_len = s->len = 102399999`, which is already far beyond the initial `MAXSTR` capacity of 1024 because repeated EOF appends kept inflating the quoted-string length.

Immediately after the unmatched opening quote is consumed, the quoted-string loop begins with the `it8->ch` value that `NextCh()` just loaded from the parser buffer; on the crashing original second parse that value is the EOF NUL.

edges.relation: The same `it8->ch` value tested by the missing EOF guard is cast to `(char)it8->ch` and passed into `StringAppend()` instead of terminating the loop.

The appended character becomes the `c` argument on the later growth-copy call; on the witnessed crash path both values are still 0, so the sink iteration is driven by the EOF byte that should have been rejected.
The first character loaded after the unmatched opening quote is the same `it8->ch` value tested by the quoted-string guard.
